chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: The feud with John Hardee over Old Black Magic
summary: Hardee, whom he let sit in during Army days, felt his solo sold Old Black Magic and quarreled over billing in Baltimore.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, we had a light feud going on, which was unexpected to me because, by me letting him sit in when he was in the army, like Charlie Parker -- same thing, no different. He used to come round, he could play, brought his horn, let him play. But he was in the Army. And when he got out of the Army I gave him some gigs. Then we made some records, I think it was ... [Old Black Magic] ... Anyhow we made it on Atlantic records and it was a hit and John's solo sold -- and we had the biggest feud and arguments because he wasn't satisfied...
... Old Black Magic ... But see his solo and the arrangement sold the tune

So he really got mad, I mean heartless mad because he didn't receive the credit that he was due and when we played another job he gave me a hard time because his name was not first. Now it's my ... recording and I let him be a part of it, but his solo ... We had the biggest feud. He wouldn't halfway play ... He got made at me in Balt'more 'cause his name was not first. Professional jealousy ... I was the one that helped him get stewed ...
